nodes.label: Cosine Noise Schedule (Nichol & Dhariwal)
nodes.rationale: Destroys information more gradually at small t; beta clipped at 0.999.

nodes.label: Noise-Prediction Parametrization (epsilon-prediction)
nodes.rationale: Target has unit scale at every t and is single-valued per (x0, eps, t), avoiding the VAE's L2 conditional-mean blur.

nodes.label: Simplified Objective L_simple
nodes.rationale: Dropping VLB per-timestep weights emphasizes harder noisier timesteps, improving sample quality.

nodes.label: DDIM Sampler (Song et al. 2021)
nodes.rationale: Non-Markovian reverse process reusing the same eps-prediction checkpoint; estimated 10-50x faster sampling without retraining.

nodes.label: EMA Weights (decay 0.9999)
nodes.rationale: Smooths weight jitter that compounds over 1000 sampling steps; but at 28,080 steps EMA retains ~6% of random init and its samples saturate (56.9% pixels), so raw weights were reported.

nodes.label: EMA Decay Warm-up / Shorter EMA Horizon
nodes.norm_label: ema decay warm-up / shorter ema horizon

nodes.label: D11: Report Results with Raw Weights
nodes.norm_label: d11: report results with raw weights
nodes.rationale: Run stopped at 80 epochs (28,080 steps); EMA 0.9999 retains ~6% random init and samples saturate; raw weights give clean samples and lower test loss (FR-015).

nodes.label: D6: EMA Validation Checkpoint Selection, Warmup, AdamW
nodes.norm_label: d6: ema validation checkpoint selection, warmup, adamw
nodes.rationale: Ho et al. settings; EMA weights are the ones used for generation.

nodes.label: D8: Resume Restores History and RNG; Exit Codes 0/1/2
nodes.norm_label: d8: resume restores history and rng; exit codes 0/1/2
nodes.rationale: Fixes two VAE defects found during parity review.

nodes.label: Unconverged EMA Sample Progression (noise to saturated blobs over 80 epochs)
nodes.norm_label: unconverged ema sample progression (noise to saturated blobs over 80 epochs)
nodes.rationale: EMA decay 0.9999 has an averaging horizon (~10k optimizer steps) that, combined with the zero-initialized output layers, keeps the EMA copy close to the untrained network for many epochs; samples go from pure noise (epoch 5) through saturated speckle (epoch 40) to high-contrast blobs (epoch 80) without recognizable CIFAR-10 objects, so reported results use raw weights instead.

nodes.label: Ho et al. (2020) Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
nodes.norm_label: ho et al. (2020) denoising diffusion probabilistic models

nodes.label: Measured 3 GB GPU Budget (Quadro T2000)
nodes.rationale: Training is compute/bandwidth-bound, not memory-bound, so official run used Colab T4 at 128x1.

nodes.label: Spatial Self-Attention at 16x16 and 8x8
nodes.rationale: Attention cost is quadratic in tokens; 32x32 too expensive for 4 GB. Uses fused scaled_dot_product_attention (~170 MiB less, ~6% faster).

nodes.label: Denoising Network epsilon_theta (time-conditioned U-Net)
nodes.rationale: U-Net gives global context at 8x8 plus pixel-exact detail via skips; widths [64,128,256] are a reduced Ho et al. model (16.06M vs 35.7M) sized for the 3 GB budget.

nodes.label: Gradient Accumulation
nodes.rationale: Trades time for GPU memory so the local T2000 (3 GB budget) reaches the same effective batch as Colab.

nodes.label: Group Normalization (32 groups)
nodes.rationale: Per-sample normalization so behavior is identical across micro-batch 32, accumulation to 128, and sampling batch 256; BatchNorm stats would differ.

nodes.label: Sinusoidal Timestep Embedding
nodes.rationale: Unique smooth code per timestep lets the network interpolate between noise levels instead of memorizing 1000 cases.

nodes.label: Nearest-Neighbor + Conv Upsampling
nodes.rationale: Avoids transposed-conv checkerboard artifacts that would be amplified over 1000 sampling steps.

nodes.label: Zero-Initialized Output Layer
nodes.rationale: Network starts near identity mapping, stabilizing early training.

nodes.label: One Code Path, Two Machines (CLI + Colab notebook)
nodes.norm_label: one code path, two machines (cli + colab notebook)
nodes.rationale: Notebook only calls the ddpm CLI, honoring the constitution's ban on notebook-only training loops.

nodes.label: D2: Two Configs (local vs Colab)
nodes.rationale: Local GPU has 3 GB budget, Colab 15 GB; only per-step batch, accumulation, workers and output_dir differ.

nodes.label: L_simple + AdamW + EMA Training Recipe
nodes.rationale: Matches Ho et al. (lr 2e-4, warmup 5000, clip 1.0, EMA 0.9999, batch 128); EMA validation makes best checkpoint track generation weights.

nodes.label: Memory Verification in verify (3072 MiB gate)
nodes.norm_label: memory verification in verify (3072 mib gate)

nodes.label: Linear & Cosine Noise Schedules
nodes.rationale: Buffers precomputed in float64 to avoid cumulative-product drift over 1000 steps; cosine β clipped at 0.999.

nodes.label: Time-Conditioned U-Net [64,128,256]
nodes.rationale: 16.06M params measured at 1,625 MiB; zero-initialized output convs start near identity for stability; nearest+conv upsampling avoids checkerboard artifacts; no 32x32 attention due to memory budget.

nodes.label: Fused SDPA Attention
nodes.rationale: 170 MiB less memory and ~6% faster; einsum kept as test reference; nn.MultiheadAttention hides projection layout.

nodes.label: fp32 Default & Dedicated Sampling Generator
nodes.rationale: fp16 was 4x slower and produced NaN on the T2000; dedicated torch.Generator gives bitwise-identical samples.

nodes.label: Zero-Init Perturbation for Gradient-Flow Check (perturb_zero_init_)
nodes.rationale: Zero-initialized output convs make the untrained network identity so upstream layers get zero gradient; checks run on a perturbed copy.

nodes.label: CIFAR-10 Dataset (45k/5k/10k split)
nodes.rationale: Parity with the VAE and the standard DDPM benchmark; normalized to [-1,1] so x_T matches N(0,I).

nodes.label: Shared Benchmark Protocol (5k vs 5k)
nodes.rationale: Identical to Hands-on VAE so numbers are comparable across repositories; not comparable to 50k-sample published FIDs.

nodes.label: D7: Index-Based Split Identical to VAE
nodes.norm_label: d7: index-based split identical to vae
nodes.rationale: Two dataset objects split by randperm indices prevent flip augmentation leaking into validation while reproducing random_split's partition.

nodes.label: Component Registry (decorator factory)
nodes.rationale: Adding a new schedule or network requires no change to training or CLI code; mirrors Hands-on VAE.

nodes.label: Linear Noise Schedule (1e-4 to 0.02)
nodes.rationale: Ho et al. CIFAR-10 setting; precomputed in float64 to avoid cumulative-product drift.

nodes.label: Closed-Form Forward Marginal q(x_t|x_0)
nodes.rationale: Any timestep reachable in one operation, so a 1000-step model trains at the cost of a normal image-to-image network.

nodes.label: Nearest-Neighbor Panel
nodes.rationale: Low FID alone cannot distinguish memorization from generalization.

nodes.label: Manual DDPM vs VAE Comparison
nodes.rationale: User decision; keeps repositories independent and avoids comparison code used once.

nodes.label: ddpm benchmark (resumable FID/IS)
nodes.rationale: --reuse-samples with manifest.json and per-batch seeded generators so resumed runs are identical and stale samples are never scored.

nodes.label: Exit Code Policy (0 success / 1 config-input / 2 runtime)
nodes.norm_label: exit code policy (0 success / 1 config-input / 2 runtime)
nodes.rationale: Fixes a gap in the VAE where exit code 2 was documented but never returned.

nodes.label: Nearest-Neighbor Panel (sample --nearest)
nodes.rationale: Option rather than a seventh command because it post-processes images sample just generated and the spec fixes the command set at six; low FID alone cannot distinguish memorization.

nodes.label: Persistent Checkpoint Schema (.pt)
nodes.rationale: model_state_dict holds full diffusion state; EMA shadow is denoiser-only; schedule buffers non-persistent and rebuilt from config.

nodes.label: Colab Training Notebook (ddpm_colab_training.ipynb)
nodes.rationale: Thin driver that only calls the CLI so it does not violate the Prohibited Patterns rule (no training loop in notebooks).

nodes.label: EMA Non-Convergence Diagnosis (6% residual init)
nodes.rationale: 0.9999^28080 ≈ 6% of init remains; errors compound over the 1000-step reverse chain even though single-step EMA loss is close.

nodes.label: Shared Benchmark Protocol (VAE parity FID/IS)
nodes.rationale: Identical Inception extractor, preprocessing, 5k samples and 10 splits make FID comparable with VAE 169.02/181.00; pytorch-fid/torchmetrics rejected for different weights.

nodes.label: Repository Parity Gap Analysis vs Hands-on VAE
nodes.norm_label: repository parity gap analysis vs hands-on vae

nodes.label: Seeded 45k/5k Split Parity with VAE random_split (D7)
nodes.norm_label: seeded 45k/5k split parity with vae random_split (d7)
nodes.rationale: Index split via randperm equals random_split partition so FID real statistics are comparable and validation is never flipped.

nodes.label: Python Interface Contracts: Registries & Base Classes
nodes.norm_label: python interface contracts: registries & base classes

nodes.label: SC-004 Risk (FID < 50 literature target)
nodes.rationale: Ho et al. report FID 3.17 with 50k samples and ~800k steps; reaching FID < 50 under the 4 GB budget may need more epochs.

nodes.label: Raw-Weights Reporting Decision
nodes.rationale: At 28,080 steps EMA 0.9999 retains ~6% of random init; EMA samples saturate (56.9% pixels at ±1) while raw samples are clean and raw test loss is lower (0.0309 vs 0.0390).

nodes.label: Zero-Based Timestep Indexing Convention
nodes.rationale: Maps directly to buffer lookups and avoids off-by-one errors; strip renderer translates to paper labels.

nodes.label: Trajectory Label Rule (label T = x_T, label k = after step k)
nodes.norm_label: trajectory label rule (label t = x_t, label k = after step k)

nodes.label: Review Gates (review-spec, review-plan)
nodes.rationale: Human approval between specify/plan and plan/tasks; rejection aborts the workflow.

nodes.label: Full SDD Cycle workflow (specify → plan → tasks → implement)
nodes.norm_label: full sdd cycle workflow (specify → plan → tasks → implement)

nodes.label: Constitution Authority (conflicts are CRITICAL)
nodes.rationale: The constitution is non-negotiable within analysis; principle changes must happen via explicit constitution update, not reinterpretation.

nodes.label: Task-ID Issue Deduplication (\bT\d{3}\b)
nodes.rationale: Prevents duplicate issues on re-runs and bounds pagination on large issue histories; never create issues in repos not matching the remote.

nodes.label: V. CLI-Driven Pipeline & Artifact Observability
nodes.rationale: All workflows exposed via modular CLIs with structured config, JSON/CSV metrics, and organized artifact directories.

nodes.label: II. Deterministic Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Seeds, hyperparameters, EMA decay and checkpoints versioned so every metric/visual is recreatable; README documents reproduction commands.

nodes.label: Ecosystem Consistency with Hands-on VAE
nodes.rationale: Layout, CLI, config schema and reporting mirror Hands-on VAE unless an ADR in docs/adr/ justifies deviation.

nodes.label: I. From-Scratch Diffusion Modeling
nodes.rationale: DDPM (Ho et al. 2020) must be authored from tensor primitives; no diffusers or pretrained pipelines; pretrained nets only inside FID/IS metrics.

nodes.label: Hardware Budget (Quadro T2000 4 GB VRAM)
nodes.rationale: No self-attention at 32x32; larger effective batches must use gradient accumulation to fit ~3.5 GB.

nodes.label: III. Standardized Benchmarking & Cross-Model Comparison
nodes.rationale: Same CIFAR-10 splits, preprocessing and FID/IS protocol as Hands-on VAE so results are directly comparable side by side.

nodes.label: IV. Test-Driven Tensor & Diffusion Mathematical Integrity
nodes.norm_label: iv. test-driven tensor & diffusion mathematical integrity
nodes.rationale: Shapes, schedule quantities, gradient flow, numerical stability and sampler determinism verified by unit tests before training.
